items.followUp: Define longitudinal strain and write its formula.

accept: change in a body s dimension
rubric.why: Strain is the ratio of a change in dimension to the original dimension.
rubric.description: Defines strain as a ratio of dimensional change to original dimension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the general definition or an equivalent formula.

rubric.why: Tensile strain is the extension per unit original length when a tensile force acts.
rubric.description: Defines tensile strain and distinguishes it from strain in general.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in length relative to the original length.

modelAnswer: Strain is the ratio of the change in a body's dimension to its original dimension.
Tensile strain is the increase in length (extension) per unit original length when a tensile force acts on the body.

items.followUp: A pump lifts 50 kg of water through a vertical height of 12 m in 8 s. Calculate its power in watts and horsepower. Take g = 9.8 m/s² and 1 hp = 746 W.

rubric.why: These are the given mass, vertical height and time in SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies the given quantities in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating m = 70 kg, h = 16 m and t = 10 s.

rubric.why: Power is work done per unit time, and the work done lifting the water is mgh.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for P = W/t = mgh/t or the equivalent steps.

rubric.why: Substituting the given values into the power formula gives the power in watts.
rubric.description: Substitutes the data into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution using the given values.

rubric.why: The calculation gives a power of 1097.6 W.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 1097.6 W or an equivalent rounded value.

rubric.why: Dividing the power in watts by 746 W per horsepower gives approximately 1.47 hp.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for approximately 1.47 hp using 1 hp = 746 W.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 70 kg, h = 16 m, t = 10 s, and g = 9.8 m/s².
Power, P = work done / time = W/t, and W = mgh; therefore P = mgh/t.
Since 1 hp = 746 W, power in horsepower = 1097.6 W / (746 W per hp).
